document.title: Meadows HK V1 Build Report — July 16, 2026
document.headline: A working intake, notification, viewer, and acknowledgement loop

workCoverage.coverageDescription: Covers the July 16, 2026 construction and verification of Meadows HK V1 as a working communication pipeline. The session refined Google Form intake, normalized submissions into JSON, established Submission_Log as append-only history, delivered alerts through a dedicated Gmail account and phone notifications, embedded a card-based response viewer in Google Sites, exposed raw JSON for inspection, implemented server-side acknowledgement, logged acknowledgement actions separately, and identified routing and task buffers as the next development phase.

subject.mainFocus: Transforming a rough Google Form experiment into a working request communication loop with structured JSON history, phone alerts, a card viewer, raw-record inspection, and acknowledgement.
subject.description: July 16, 2026 work update documenting the first working version of the Meadows HK request, notification, review, and acknowledgement system.

narrative.promptingSituation: The Meadows HK request system was still a rough Google Form experiment. Form branching created messy response columns, work notifications competed with personal email, and submissions lacked a dependable human-readable review and response loop.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: The raw response sheet did not need to become the operational interface. Apps Script could normalize each submission into JSON, preserve it in an append-only log, and derive alerts, cards, and acknowledgement actions without rewriting the source.
narrative.intendedOutcome: Create a usable V1 communication pipeline that captures unexpected requests, preserves structured evidence, alerts the phone, displays readable records, allows raw inspection, and records acknowledgement.
narrative.approach: Simplify the form while retaining flexible Other options; normalize nonblank submitted fields; write one JSON record to Submission_Log; send alerts to a dedicated Gmail account; embed a card viewer in Google Sites; add raw JSON inspection; implement acknowledgement as a server-side action; log that action separately; and test every layer.

progression.title: Refined the intake form
progression.description: Reduced top-level routes, preserved location detail, and retained Other options for edge cases.
progression.result: Unexpected requests could still be captured coherently without perfect advance categorization.

progression.title: Created normalized permanent records
progression.description: Apps Script ignored blank branch fields and stored the useful submission as JSON in Submission_Log.
progression.result: Messy form responses were converted into flexible, inspectable, append-only history.

progression.title: Established a dedicated alert channel
progression.description: Notifications were sent to an alternate Gmail account configured to alert the phone for every message.
progression.result: The email became an alarm signal while the Responses page remained the actual work surface.

progression.title: Built the response card viewer
progression.description: An Apps Script web app embedded in Google Sites displayed recent submissions as cards with metadata, answered fields, raw JSON, and an acknowledgement control.
progression.result: Structured records became readable while retaining direct access to their exact JSON.

progression.title: Implemented acknowledgement
progression.description: The browser sent submission_id to Apps Script, which resolved the source record, sent a test email, appended Acknowledgement_Log, and changed the card state.
progression.result: The system proved that actions could be performed and logged without disturbing Submission_Log.

progression.title: Extracted V2 design pressures
progression.description: Observed form branching, edge cases, card readability, raw JSON value, dedicated alerts, and manual routing.
progression.result: Future work was grounded in real V1 behavior rather than speculative redesign.

problemsEncountered.problem: Google Form branching produced a wide, messy response sheet.
problemsEncountered.effect: The raw sheet was difficult to treat as a stable operational record or readable work surface.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Apps Script ignored blank branch fields and created a normalized JSON record in Submission_Log.

problemsEncountered.problem: Work alerts were mixed with personal email.
problemsEncountered.effect: New submissions could be overlooked and the personal inbox became part of the operational workflow.
problemsEncountered.resolution: A separate Gmail account became the Meadows alert inbox and the phone was configured for every-message notification.

problemsEncountered.problem: The system had no response action beyond viewing a submission.
problemsEncountered.effect: A reviewer could inspect a request but could not record that it had been received.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Added a server-connected Acknowledge button and separate Acknowledgement_Log.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Attempt to enumerate every possible request category in advance.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: Detailed categories appeared likely to improve organization.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: Real requests include edge cases that do not fit a complete predefined list.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Reliable location, description, original evidence, and flexible Other routes matter more than perfect taxonomy.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Treat the Form Responses sheet as the useful operational record.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: It already contained all submitted values.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: Branch-generated blank columns made the sheet structurally noisy and difficult to read.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Raw intake can remain messy when a normalized record layer is created afterward.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Use email as the primary work surface.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: Email is an immediate notification and communication channel.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: Email is less suitable than a card viewer for reviewing structured records and source JSON.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: The email only needs to signal that work exists; the viewer should remain the work surface.

turningPoints.title: Submission_Log became the permanent record
turningPoints.description: The system separated raw form intake from normalized, append-only submission history.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Every later view and action could be derived without rewriting the source.

turningPoints.title: The alert and work surface were separated
turningPoints.description: Dedicated Gmail and phone notifications were assigned the alert role, while the Responses page handled review.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: The communication system became clearer and less dependent on inbox management.

turningPoints.title: Acknowledgement proved the action pattern
turningPoints.description: A card button successfully called server-side Apps Script and created a separate action record.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: The viewer became a foundation for later routing and task controls rather than a passive display.

keyDecisions.reason: It must remain the permanent receipt of what entered the system.
alternativesConsidered: Update the submission row when acknowledged

keyDecisions.decision: Store normalized JSON in one log cell.
keyDecisions.reason: JSON can preserve varied form responses without forcing every branch into a fixed wide table.
alternativesConsidered: Use only the raw Form Responses row
Create fixed columns for every possible branch
consequences: The record remains flexible and inspectable.
Cards and future routing can use the same source object.

keyDecisions.decision: Use a dedicated Gmail account only as an alert channel.
keyDecisions.reason: Operational notifications should remain separate from personal email, and the viewer is a better review surface.
alternativesConsidered: Continue sending alerts to personal Gmail
consequences: The Responses page retained the full operational context.

keyDecisions.decision: Send acknowledgements to a safe test address.
keyDecisions.reason: The server action and email loop needed verification before contacting a supervisor.
consequences: Testing could proceed without accidental external communication.

keyDecisions.decision: Keep V1 in use while V2 is learned from it.
keyDecisions.reason: Observed use provides better requirements than redesigning from imagination.
alternativesConsidered: Replace V1 immediately because it is imperfect
consequences: Future architecture can be based on actual pressures and edge cases.

narrative.methodEstablished: Capture broadly, normalize after intake, preserve immutable JSON history, derive human-readable views and action logs, separate alerts from work surfaces, test with safe targets, and let working V1 usage determine V2.
narrative.result: Meadows HK V1 became a usable intake, notification, review, raw-record inspection, and acknowledgement system.
lessonsLearned: Form categories can remain imperfect when the original submission and flexible description are preserved.
Messy intake does not require a messy permanent record.
JSON provides a durable bridge between variable form input and readable interfaces.
Cards are better for human review than raw spreadsheet rows.
Raw JSON should remain available for confidence and debugging.
Email can function as an alert without becoming the work surface.
A simple action button can establish the pattern for future routing.
Working systems reveal better next-version requirements than speculative redesign.
narrative.directionChange: The project moved from a form experiment to a working communication system and established routing buffers as the next phase.
narrative.narrativeSummary: The July 16 V1 session connected form intake, normalized JSON, append-only history, dedicated alerts, a Google Sites card viewer, raw-record inspection, and a separately logged acknowledgement action into one complete communication loop.
